description: Notification mirroring vectors (changelog 56). Spec: docs/protocol.md, "Notifications: notif.*". The PC runs everything except the Android-only arrays; the phone runs everything except where a row says PC.
howToRead: limits: every limit of the spec in one place. nid[]: key -> nid (first 32 hex of SHA-256 of the UTF-8 key). iconHash[]: PNG bytes (base64url) -> hash. icon[]: a notif.icon frame is built from hash and png (or pngFile, a path relative to protocol/) and expect says accepted, dropped (silently, counted) or bad_request. clean[]: field + input -> expected after the five steps (null = absent); the limit comes from limits (messageSender, messageText, line, hint and label are the inner fields). post[]: cases in the format of messages.json (from, to, state, own and peer = the capabilities of the receiver's own latest hello and of the sender's), expect.notif is the normalized post: every field present with its default (group, silent, sensitive, redacted false; importance 3), an absent optional string omitted, empty arrays omitted. code[]: the PC's check of a code. toastIds[] and toastArguments[]: how the PC names a toast and parses the arguments of a click. rate[]: limiter pc (bucket 20, refill 1 per second, identical post within 2 s ignored, rate_limited errors one per 10 s) and phone (bucket 10, refill 1 per 500 ms, 20 posts per 60 s per package, removes up to 50 per 10 s); events are in time order, expect lists one outcome per event. coalesce[]: the phone's per-nid sender (events in time order; expect.sent is what goes on the wire, with its time). sendNotif[]: whether a sender may send a notif.* message to a peer whose accepted hellos are given. syncDiff[]: which toasts a notif.sync removes. toastLabel[]: a hint or a button label in the form it has on the toast, which is the form the PC sends back in notif.action.label and the phone compares (run by both sides). otpDetect[], redactedText, skip[] and pickActions[] are run by the phone only (their format is in protocol/README.md). All non-ASCII characters are written as escapes.

post.name: post-redacted-with-nothing-else
post.note: no title, text, messages or lines, but redacted: accepted

post.name: post-messages-text-and-sender-are-cleaned-and-cut
post.note: an empty sender is 'You' (absent); a message with no text left is dropped

post.name: post-code-lowercase-is-ignored
post.note: never bad_request: no button, the notification is still shown

post.name: post-code-is-not-cleaned-first
post.note: checked as sent: whitespace around it makes it invalid, it is not trimmed

post.name: post-empty-subtext-and-conversation-do-not-count
post.note: only title, text, bigText, messages and lines count as content

post.name: post-over-32-KiB-is-too-large
post.note: the 32 KiB rule is on the whole frame, before the strings are cut

post.name: post-exactly-32-KiB-is-accepted

rate.name: pc-a-burst-of-25-distinct-posts-uses-the-bucket
rate.note: capacity 20: the first 20 are accepted, the rest dropped; one rate_limited error, at the first drop

rate.name: pc-refills-one-per-second
rate.note: at 999 ms there is 0.999 of a token: dropped; at 1000 one is there; at 3000 two have refilled

rate.name: pc-identical-post-within-2-seconds-is-ignored
rate.note: the same payload for the same nid within 2 s of the last accepted one is ignored and uses no token; at exactly 2 s it is new; a different payload is new

rate.name: pc-a-duplicate-does-not-use-a-token
rate.note: 30 repeats cost nothing, so 19 more distinct posts still fit (1 + 19 = 20)

rate.name: pc-rate-limited-errors-are-at-most-one-per-10-seconds
rate.note: ten posts a second for 30 s drains the bucket: the first drop sends an error, and the next one may come 10 s later

rate.name: pc-a-dropped-post-is-not-remembered-as-the-last-accepted
rate.note: the post at 500 is dropped (no token); the same payload at 1000 is not a duplicate of it: it takes the token that has refilled

rate.name: phone-a-burst-of-12-posts-uses-the-budget
rate.note: capacity 10: ten sent, two dropped for the budget (the package cap is not reached)

rate.name: phone-package-cap-is-20-per-60-seconds
rate.note: one post per 600 ms keeps the global budget healthy; the 21st within 60 s from the same package is dropped for the package cap, and another package is still served

rate.name: phone-package-cap-window-slides
rate.note: 20 sent in the first 19 s; the window is (t - 60 s, t]: at 20 s and 59.999 s the package is full; at 60 s the post made at 0 has just left, so one fits; at 60.001 it is full again

rate.name: phone-a-package-over-its-cap-does-not-use-the-budget
rate.note: ten dropped posts of p cost no tokens, so q can still send ten

rate.name: phone-removes-are-exempt-from-the-bucket-up-to-50-per-10-seconds
rate.note: the bucket is empty, removes go anyway; 50 in 10 s, the 51st and 52nd are dropped; at 10100 the first of them (t = 100) has left the window

coalesce.name: a-burst-sends-the-first-and-then-the-last-when-the-second-ends
coalesce.note: a at 0; b, c and d replace each other; d goes out at 1000

coalesce.name: a-pending-post-equal-to-the-last-sent-is-dropped
coalesce.note: the last state is 'a', which is what the PC already has: nothing goes out at 1000

coalesce.name: the-window-is-one-second-from-the-last-send
coalesce.note: b is sent at 1000 (the window of a ends); c at 2500 is 1500 ms after that: at once; d waits until 3500

coalesce.name: a-remove-for-a-nid-with-nothing-pending
coalesce.note: after a remove the same content is new again, and is sent at once

coalesce.name: many-updates-in-one-window-send-two-posts-in-all
coalesce.note: 50 updates in 735 ms: the first at once and the last at 1000

toastLabel.name: two-in-a-row-are-two-spaces
toastLabel.note: no collapsing: only the five steps of clean collapse

toastLabel.name: only-separators-is-empty
toastLabel.note: a button with such a label is not shown; a reply with such a hint has no hint
